text: Lesson 26 decided the shape of this integration: an event-driven webhook trigger, followed by a REST Message pull back to Meridian HR for the real data. This lesson builds the two pieces that make that pull possible — real OAuth 2.0 authentication, and the REST Message itself.

The OAuth Entity Profile is where the real credentials live: a Client Credentials grant type, Meridian HR's token URL, an encrypted client ID and secret, and a read-only scope. Attach this profile to the REST Message, and RESTMessageV2 requests and refreshes its own bearer token automatically — no manual header, ever.

Chapter 3 covered three options. Basic Auth sends a password on every request — Meridian HR doesn't even accept it anymore. Authorization Code grant assumes a human user logging in and delegating access, and there's no human here. Client Credentials grant exists exactly for this case: two systems, a client ID and secret, no user in the loop.

The REST Message itself follows the same pattern Lessons 4 and 5 built, just pointed at a real endpoint: a GET to Meridian HR's employees endpoint, with the employee ID as a placeholder, and OAuth 2.0 set as the authentication type right on the Function record.

In script, a Script Include method names the REST Message and Function, fills in the employeeId placeholder, executes the call, and checks the status code before parsing the body as JSON. Nothing about OAuth appears here at all — the profile attached to the REST Message record handles the token entirely on its own.

The Scripted REST API resource that receives Meridian HR's webhook calls this same method the instant a notification arrives, then acknowledges with a 202. At this integration's low new-hire volume, pulling the record inline here is honest and simple — a much higher-volume feed would queue that pull onto an async Business Rule instead.

Authentication and the pull are real now. Lesson 28 makes this production-grade: exponential backoff when Meridian HR fails, an idempotency check before any sys_user gets created twice, and structured logging at every checkpoint.
